![](../../src/images/hex_complex.png){.intro_image fig-alt="Course logo"}

Welcome to **GIS in R: Fundamentals and applications for ecologists**! In this course, we will explore the core skills necessary to begin using R as a GIS. You will also gain an in-depth understanding of how to apply the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/packages/){target="_blank"} to efficiently wrangle spatial data. Throughout this course, we will focus on how to seamlessly integrate GIS applications into a modern R workflow and explore new ways of thinking about ecological data.

*Note: Please download this file and open it in your web browser.*

## Module overview

In this first module, we will cover the basic concepts and primary tools that we will use in this course. We will not be working with much real data yet (but soon will!). Instead, this module is really dedicated to developing a conceptual understanding of R that we can build on throughout the course. It is divided into five sections:

-   **1.1 Course introduction**: A general introduction to the content of this course, where to find course resources, and how to navigate course content.
-   **1.2 Getting started**: This section provides the [*necessary*]{style="color:red;"} steps that you must take *prior* to completing the content of this module.
-   **1.3 Objects**: This lesson is an enhanced review of functions, environments, and common data objects. Special emphasis is placed on developing a vocabulary that will give you the flexibility to address and understand more complex operations.
-   **1.4 Importing, exploring, and exporting data**: Here, we will review how to import and export [.csv]{.mono} and [.rds]{.mono} files, learn how to read [.xlsx]{.mono} files, and describe exploratory steps that should be taken *every time* you read a file.
-   **1.5 Assignments**: In this lesson, we will review global (and "local") assignments, and you will learn the benefits and pitfalls of their usage. Along the way, you will learn how to use magrittr's pipe operator, and I will provide recommendations to improve your R workflow and manage your global environment.

**Problem set** (due 30 Aug): R foundations

*Note: We will quickly build on the content herein, so please be sure to read/view all content in the order that it appears!*

## Readings and resources

Please review the following resources:

-   **[Course style guide](https://evansbrians.github.io/gis_2026/resources/course_style_guide/){target="_blank"}**: Modern standards in R coding compel us to generate code that is consistent, parsimonious, and communicable. This tutorial provides the set of code formatting rules that I ask you to follow in the course. The provided rules are closely aligned with the tidyverse style guide.
-   **[Solving and submitting problem sets](https://evansbrians.github.io/gis_2026/resources/solving_and_submitting_problem_sets/){target="_blank"}**: This brief tutorial provides tips and tricks for completing our notoriously difficult weekly problem sets with as little pain as possible.
